mechanism_narrative: A rising FEDFUNDS rate above 5% for two consecutive months predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened policy discounting future earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in all FEDFUNDS > 5.0 regimes, or FEDFUNDS decline occurs but no return reversal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (monthly employment) coinciding with a decline in UNRATE predicts stronger consumer demand and positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
regime_hint: expansionary labor market with falling unemployment
failure_condition: No significant return advantage in 60-day windows where PAYEMS up >10% and UNRATE down >0.2pp, or correlation <0.3.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in GDPC1 (real private consumption) of at least 3% for three consecutive months predicts positive S&P 20-day forward returns as it signals robust economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth > 3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain flat or negative during qualifying GDPC1 upswings, or the effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 for two consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative during INDPRO contraction periods, or the effect is not detectable in walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4.0% for four consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive as policy remains accommodative.
failure_condition: No positive 20-day returns in such regimes, or FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0 before returns materialize.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in UNRATE below 3.5% and a rise in PAYEMS above 155,000 suggests labor market improvement that boosts equity valuations, predicting positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS > 155000 in the same month
regime_hint: labor market softening turning to strengthening
failure_condition: No significant return advantage in 60-day windows meeting the trigger, or interaction p-value >0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in HOUST (household spending) growth exceeding 2% after a prior month of >1% suggests momentum building, leading to positive 20-day S&P returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly growth accelerates past 2% after >1% prior month
failure_condition: No positive 20-day returns during qualifying acceleration phases, or effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in RSAFS (retail sales) of over 5% indicate weakening consumer demand, forecasting negative S&P 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly decline >5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative during qualifying declines, or the signal is not robust across multiple cycles.
